findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Name the document explicitly, for example "a printed copy of the budget summary" or "of this policy," or remove the sentence if it is not needed here.
findings.violation: It is unclear what "a printed copy" refers to. The preceding sentence only says the benefits team tracks the stipend budget, and no document has been named yet that staff could request a printed copy of.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the people operations office updates the equipment catalog each quarter."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral connector, or start a new paragraph, for example "Separately, the people operations office updates the equipment catalog each quarter."
findings.violation: "Similarly" signals that this sentence parallels the one before it, but tracking a budget and updating a catalog are unrelated actions performed by different teams, so the connector misrepresents the relationship between the two sentences.

findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time."
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for the benefit throughout, or state explicitly that "workspace stipend" and "equipment stipend" refer to the same thing.
findings.location: Eligibility section, third paragraph, first sentence
findings.violation: The document names the benefit "home-office equipment stipend" in the title and in the first eligibility paragraph, then switches to "workspace stipend" here without saying whether this is the same program or a different one.

findings.evidence: nine sentences run together without separation, including "The workspace must sit inside the employee's primary residence for the stipend to apply." and "A workspace located in a shared coworking space does not qualify for the stipend under this section."
findings.fix: Convert the paragraph into a bulleted checklist, with one eligibility criterion per bullet.
findings.violation: The paragraph itself states the reviewer "checks one at a time," describing a checklist, but the criteria are presented as a single undifferentiated block of prose, which makes the individual conditions hard to locate and verify.

findings.evidence: "However, an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: State the specific starting point for the three day count, for example "three days after the request is marked incomplete."
findings.violation: It is not stated whether the three days is counted from the original submission date or from the date the request was marked incomplete, so a reader cannot determine when to expect the reminder.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Replace "shall" with "must" to match the rest of the document.
findings.violation: "Shall" is a formal register that does not appear anywhere else in the document, which otherwise uses "must," so the sentence reads as if it were copied from a different source and breaks the document's otherwise consistent tone.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests." versus "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: State in "How to Apply" whether a photo of the receipt satisfies the submission requirement, and cross reference the "Required Documentation" section.
findings.location: Required Documentation section, second sentence, compared with How to Apply section, first sentence
findings.violation: It is unclear whether the receipt required before review begins in "How to Apply" can be a photo, as later permitted in "Required Documentation," creating an apparent conflict about what form of receipt is acceptable.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount. Also, unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year."
findings.fix: Add the actual reimbursement amount or cap covered by the stipend, or rename the section to describe what it actually contains, for example "Reimbursement Review Process."
findings.violation: A section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never states a dollar figure, percentage, or cap, so a reader looking for the actual reimbursement amount finds nothing responsive to the heading.

findings.evidence: "The applicant must keep the equipment in good working condition and this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Name the specific office responsible for the photo check, for example "the benefits team may ask for a brief photo check."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: "This office" has no clear antecedent. The document mentions the benefits team, the people operations office, and the finance office elsewhere, and it does not say which of these performs the photo check.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device..."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly" or replace it with a new heading or bullet separating the two distinct rules.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second paragraph, first word
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this sentence parallels the previous one about photo checks, but a device count rule is not similar to a compliance photo check, so the connector misleads the reader about how the two sentences relate.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Split the sentence into separate sentences, one per rule, for example stating the base rule, then the exception condition, then how the exception is tracked, as three short sentences.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second paragraph
findings.violation: This single sentence combines at least four separate ideas, the one device per category rule, the fieldwork exception, the approval requirement, and the tracking method, into roughly eighty words, which makes it very difficult to parse and to verify each rule individually.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Rewrite the section in third person to match the rest of the document, for example "The employee records the stipend item on the request form."
findings.location: Terminology Notes section, first three sentences
findings.violation: The document uses third person throughout, for example "the employee" and "the manager," but this section abruptly switches to second person "you," which is inconsistent and leaves it unclear whether "you" always means the employee.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated process description here, or move any new information into "How to Apply" and limit this section to defining terms.
findings.violation: This restates, in different words, information already given in the "How to Apply" section about submitting through the portal, without adding new information, under a heading that suggests term definitions rather than process steps.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: List the full sequence of steps here to match "How to Apply," or remove this section if it duplicates that one.
findings.violation: This section lists only two steps, but the earlier "How to Apply" section describes additional required steps, including the approval form, the purchase order, and reviewing the confirmation summary, so "Request Steps" is incomplete relative to the process already described.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time." compared with the Program Overview section's "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Replace this section with actual special case scenarios, for example contractor eligibility or remote international staff, or remove the duplicated text.
findings.violation: A section headed "Special Cases" contains no special case scenarios. Instead it repeats the Program Overview text almost verbatim, with only "benefits team" swapped for "finance liaison" and "tracks" for "reviews," so it does not deliver the content its heading promises.

findings.evidence: "The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Rewrite in active voice naming the responsible party, and define "repeat request" and "escalation," for example stating who escalates a request, to whom, and after how many submissions.
findings.violation: Both sentences use nominalized, agentless phrasing that hides who performs the action, and "escalation of repeat requests" is never defined anywhere in the document, so a reader cannot tell what counts as a repeat request or where an escalation goes.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit." compared with the near identical sentences in the Program Overview and Special Cases sections.
findings.fix: Replace this section with contact information for questions and a description of how policy updates are communicated, or remove it if it is redundant with the other two sections.
findings.violation: A section titled "Questions and Updates" would be expected to explain how to ask questions or where to find policy updates, but instead it repeats budget tracking language already given, with variations, in "Program Overview" and "Special Cases," so it answers no question and describes no update process.
